sections.name: Frontend - React & Modern JS
sections.explanation_simple: React is the most popular way to build websites today. Instead of the old way (loading a new HTML page for every click), React updates only the parts of the page that change - making everything feel fast and app-like. Everything in React is a 'component' - a reusable piece of UI like a button, a form, or a whole page. Components can hold 'state' (data that changes, like a counter or form input) and respond to 'props' (data passed from parent components). Think of components as Lego bricks that snap together to build complex UIs.
key_concepts: Component: A reusable piece of UI (function returning JSX)
JSX: HTML-like syntax in JavaScript (looks like HTML, but it's JavaScript)
Props: Data passed TO a component (like function arguments)
State: Data that belongs TO a component (can change over time)
useState: Hook that adds state to a component
useEffect: Hook for side effects (API calls, timers, subscriptions)
Virtual DOM: React's smart way of updating only what changed
SPA: Single Page Application (one HTML page, JS handles everything)
Next.js: React framework with server-side rendering (SEO friendly)
TypeScript: JavaScript with types (catches bugs before they happen)

sections.learning_path: HTML/CSS basics -> JavaScript fundamentals (ES6+) -> React basics (create-react-app) -> Next.js (full framework) -> TypeScript -> State management -> Advanced patterns

sections.name: Backend - Node.js, Python & Databases
sections.explanation_simple: The backend is the 'engine room' of a website - it stores data, handles authentication, processes payments, and serves content to the frontend. It runs on a server (not in the browser) and communicates with the frontend through APIs. Node.js lets you use JavaScript on the server (so you know one language for everything), FastAPI/Django let you use Python (great for data-heavy apps), and both can talk to databases like PostgreSQL or MongoDB.
key_concepts: REST API: Standard way for frontend to talk to backend (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
Express/FastAPI: Web frameworks for building APIs quickly
CRUD: Create, Read, Update, Delete (the four basic database operations)
SQL: Structured Query Language (talking to relational databases like PostgreSQL)
NoSQL: Non-relational databases (MongoDB stores JSON-like documents)
ORM: Object-Relational Mapping (Prisma, SQLAlchemy - database without writing SQL)
Authentication: Passwords, JWT tokens, OAuth (login with Google/GitHub)
Middleware: Code that runs between request and response (auth checks, logging)
WebSockets: Real-time two-way communication (chat, live updates, games)

code_examples.title: FastAPI Backend with PostgreSQL
code_examples.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import List, Optional
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, Boolean
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker

# Database setup
DATABASE_URL = "postgresql://user:password@localhost/todoapp"
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base = declarative_base()

# Database model
class TodoDB(Base):
    __tablename__ = "todos"
    
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    text = Column(String, nullable=False)
    completed = Column(Boolean, default=False)

# Create tables
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

# Pydantic schemas (for API validation)
class TodoCreate(BaseModel):
    text: str

class TodoUpdate(BaseModel):
    completed: bool

class TodoResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    text: str
    completed: bool
    
    class Config:
        from_attributes = True

# FastAPI app
app = FastAPI(title="Todo API", version="1.0")

# Dependency to get DB session
def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

# CRUD Endpoints
@app.get("/todos", response_model=List[TodoResponse])
def get_todos(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(TodoDB).all()

@app.post("/todos", response_model=TodoResponse, status_code=201)
def create_todo(todo: TodoCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = TodoDB(text=todo.text)
    db.add(db_todo)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

@app.put("/todos/{todo_id}", response_model=TodoResponse)
def update_todo(todo_id: int, todo: TodoUpdate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = db.query(TodoDB).filter(TodoDB.id == todo_id).first()
    if not db_todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    db_todo.completed = todo.completed
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_todo)
    return db_todo

@app.delete("/todos/{todo_id}", status_code=204)
def delete_todo(todo_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_todo = db.query(TodoDB).filter(TodoDB.id == todo_id).first()
    if not db_todo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Todo not found")
    db.delete(db_todo)
    db.commit()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

code_examples.title: Docker Compose for Full Stack
code_examples.code:
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  # Frontend
  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
    depends_on:
      - backend
  
  # Backend
  backend:
    build: ./backend
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@db:5432/todoapp
    depends_on:
      - db
  
  # Database
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=user
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password
      - POSTGRES_DB=todoapp
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"

volumes:
  postgres_data:

sections.learning_path: Node.js/Express basics -> REST API design -> Database setup (PostgreSQL) -> Authentication (JWT) -> ORM (Prisma/SQLAlchemy) -> FastAPI or Django for Python -> Docker deployment

sections.name: Databases - SQL & NoSQL
sections.explanation_simple: Databases store your app's data permanently. Think of SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL) as a spreadsheet with strict rules - every row has specific columns, you can do complex math and filtering, and everything is connected through IDs. NoSQL (MongoDB, Redis) is more like a folder of JSON files - very flexible, each document can have different fields, and it's faster for certain use cases. SQL is usually better for complex data relationships (user -> orders -> products), while NoSQL is better for simple, fast, or huge-scale data.
key_concepts: PostgreSQL: Most powerful open-source SQL database (used by Instagram, Reddit)
MySQL: Very popular SQL database (used by Facebook, YouTube, Twitter originally)
MongoDB: Document database (stores JSON-like documents, very flexible)
Redis: In-memory cache/database (super fast, stores key-value pairs)
SQL Queries: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, JOIN, GROUP BY
Indexes: Speed up searches (like a book's index, makes queries 100x faster)
Migrations: Version control for your database schema (changing table structures)
Normalization: Organizing data to avoid duplication
Transactions: Multiple operations that must all succeed or all fail (money transfer)

code_examples.title: SQL Queries for a Game Database
code_examples.code:
-- Create tables for a game leaderboard system

CREATE TABLE players (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_login TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE scores (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    player_id INTEGER REFERENCES players(id),
    score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (score >= 0),
    level_reached INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
    time_played_seconds INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    achieved_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_scores_player ON scores(player_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_scores_value ON scores(score DESC);

-- Insert a player
INSERT INTO players (username, email) 
VALUES ('ProGamer99', 'pro@example.com');

-- Insert a score
INSERT INTO scores (player_id, score, level_reached, time_played_seconds)
VALUES (1, 15000, 12, 3600);

-- Get the leaderboard (top 10 players)
SELECT 
    p.username,
    MAX(s.score) as best_score,
    MAX(s.level_reached) as max_level,
    COUNT(s.id) as games_played
FROM players p
JOIN scores s ON p.id = s.player_id
GROUP BY p.id, p.username
ORDER BY best_score DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Get player stats
SELECT 
    p.username,
    s.score,
    s.level_reached,
    s.achieved_at
FROM players p
JOIN scores s ON p.id = s.player_id
WHERE p.username = 'ProGamer99'
ORDER BY s.score DESC
LIMIT 1;

-- Average score per level
SELECT 
    level_reached,
    AVG(score) as avg_score,
    COUNT(*) as attempts
FROM scores
GROUP BY level_reached
ORDER BY level_reached;

sections.learning_path: Learn SQL basics (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) -> Table design (normalization) -> JOINs -> Indexes -> PostgreSQL -> ORM (Prisma/TypeORM) -> MongoDB for NoSQL -> Redis for caching

sections.name: DevOps & Deployment
sections.explanation_simple: DevOps is how you get your code from your laptop to the internet where people can use it. In the old days, you'd copy files to a server by hand. Today, it's an automated pipeline: you push code to GitHub, tests run automatically, Docker packages your app into a 'container' (like a shipping container that works everywhere), and it deploys to cloud servers. This automation means you can update your website 100 times a day without breaking anything.
key_concepts: CI/CD: Continuous Integration (auto-test code) / Continuous Deployment (auto-release)
Docker: Packages your app with everything it needs to run (no "but it works on my machine!")
Kubernetes: Orchestrates multiple Docker containers (scales to millions of users)
GitHub Actions: Automate tasks when you push code (test, build, deploy)
Cloud Providers: AWS (biggest), Google Cloud, Azure, Vercel (easiest for frontend)
Nginx: Web server that routes traffic, handles SSL, load balancing
SSL/TLS: Encrypts traffic between user and server (padlock icon in browser)
Domain + DNS: Your website name (google.com) points to your server IP
Monitoring: Tracking errors, performance, and uptime (Datadog, Sentry)

code_examples.title: GitHub Actions CI/CD Pipeline
code_examples.code:
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: testpass
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:testpass@localhost:5432/postgres
  
  deploy:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build -t myapp .
      
      - name: Push to container registry
        run: |
          docker tag myapp registry.example.com/myapp:latest
          docker push registry.example.com/myapp:latest
      
      - name: Deploy to server
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.SERVER_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SERVER_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            docker pull registry.example.com/myapp:latest
            docker-compose up -d
            docker system prune -f

sections.learning_path: Git and GitHub -> Basic server management -> Docker containers -> Docker Compose -> CI/CD (GitHub Actions) -> Cloud deployment (AWS/Vercel) -> Kubernetes for scaling
